elements.element: The aggregate liability cap applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: New 10.9: "each Party's aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed..." — symmetrical in party direction, and no residual unlimited-Customer-liability language exists elsewhere.

elements.element: The cap is the greater of fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim and USD 1,000,000.
elements.evidence: 10.9 caps at "the fees paid or payable by the Company ... in the twelve (12) months preceding the claim" only; the greater-of USD 1,000,000 floor is absent. Defect: no alternative fixed-amount limb.

elements.element: The exclusion of indirect and consequential damages applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: No exclusion-of-damages sentence anywhere in the rendered text; 10.9 addresses only the aggregate cap. Defect: missing mutual indirect/consequential/special damages exclusion.

elements.element: Breach of confidentiality obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: "Excluded Claims" expressly includes "its breach of its confidentiality obligations", and the cap applies "Except for Excluded Claims".

elements.element: Breach of data protection and security obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: Excluded Claims list omits data protection and security obligations. Defect: add "its breach of its data protection or security obligations" to the Excluded Claims definition.
Excluded Claims expressly includes "a Party's indemnification obligations", which sit outside the cap.
Fraud is absent from the Excluded Claims definition in 10.9. Defect: add "fraud" to the carve-out list.

elements.element: Infringement of the other party's intellectual property is uncapped.
elements.evidence: No IP-infringement carve-out in Excluded Claims. Defect: add "its infringement of the other Party's intellectual property rights".

elements.element: Customer payment obligations are excluded from damages subject to the cap.
elements.evidence: 10.9 contains no statement that the Company's payment/fee obligations are not "damages" subject to the cap. Defect: add an express sentence excluding Customer's payment obligations from the capped amount.

elements.element: The aggregate liability cap applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: 10.9 applies the cap to "each Party's aggregate liability"; no one-sided or Customer-uncapped language survives elsewhere in the Agreement.

elements.element: The cap is based on 12 months of fees.
elements.evidence: "shall not exceed the fees paid or payable by the Company under this Agreement in the twelve (12) months preceding the claim" — a 12-month fee basis, above the 6-month walk-away floor.
"Excluded Claims" means a Party's indemnification obligations ... and the cap operates "Except for Excluded Claims", so indemnities sit outside the cap.

elements.element: Breach of confidentiality obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: Excluded Claims expressly captures "its breach of its confidentiality obligations".
Excluded Claims expressly captures "its gross negligence".
Excluded Claims expressly captures "its wilful misconduct".

reasons: Fallback checklist is complete: the inserted Section 10.9 gives a mutual aggregate cap at twelve months' fees paid or payable by the Company, with indemnification, confidentiality breach, gross negligence and wilful misconduct expressly outside the cap via a self-contained "Excluded Claims" definition.

Preferred level is not reached because the clause omits the greater-of USD 1,000,000 limb, the mutual indirect/consequential damages exclusion, and carve-outs for data protection/security breach, fraud and infringement of the other Party's IP, and it does not state that the Company's payment obligations are not damages subject to the cap. The drafter would need to amend the cap sentence to "the greater of (a) ... and (b) USD 1,000,000", add a mutual consequential-damages exclusion sentence, extend the Excluded Claims list, and add the payment-obligations carve-out.

Minimality holds: the Agreement had no liability language at all (Section 9 is limited to authority warranties; 10.1-10.8 are boilerplate), so a concise insertion is appropriate. No existing wording was deleted or paraphrased, and the insertion adds no survival tail, procedure, expense allocation or other extra requirement beyond the six fallback elements.

Intent is preserved: 10.9 sits after 10.8 within Section 10, which already survives under 10.7; "Excluded Claims" is defined in-line; "Company" is an existing Customer alias; no cross-reference is left dangling and no retained sentence contradicts the new cap.
